label: VERIFIED
extraction: Loop Design Check five-point goal framework. 1) Done-criterion is machine-verifiable. 2) Boundary conditions defined alongside done-criterion (what it must NOT do) - anti-Goodhart; missing boundaries = license to cheat. 3) Has failure fallback - retry cap N + escalate to human when exceeded. 4) Goal is layered. 5) Prefer reconciliation over assertion for done-criterion - anchor to external fact (golden sample / upstream total / financial tie-out / platform back-office numbers) before own assertions. 'All tests pass' can be gamed (loosen asserts, fake mocks, swallow exceptions); 'diff vs reference < 0.01' can't. Self-check: read goal to someone who doesn't know domain - can they run one command and tell whether it's done? If not, it isn't decidable enough. Bad goals: vague ('make it good', 'write it sharper') - comparator can't judge -> either never passes (stuck retrying) or guesses (passes/blocks at random). Good goals: decidable ('all 96 unit tests green AND change-list produced', 'module-02 fields filled, pytest passes, business logic untouched').
